keyVerseText: Jehoiakim was twenty and five years old when he began to reign; and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. And his mother's name was Zebudah, the daughter of Pedaiah of Rumah.
rootMeaning: The root of זְבִידָה (Zebudah) is זָבַד (zâbad), which primarily means to confer or bestow. This root conveys the idea of giving or endowing something valuable. The feminine form זְבִידָה thus literally means "given," emphasizing the concept of being a gift or something bestowed. This etymology enriches the common English gloss of Zebudah as a proper name by highlighting the underlying notion of divine or gracious giving.
usageInScripture: The word זְבִידָה appears only once in Scripture, specifically as the name of the mother of Jehoiakim, a king of Judah, in 2 Kings 23:36. It is consistently translated as the proper name Zebudah, without variation or metaphorical extension. This singular usage as a personal name grounds the word in a historical and genealogical context, illustrating how names in Scripture often carry significant meaning related to their root words.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding זְבִידָה as meaning "given" invites reflection on the biblical theme of God’s gifts and providence. As the mother of a king, Zebudah symbolizes the human vessel through whom God’s sovereign plans unfold, reminding believers that God’s blessings and appointments are graciously bestowed. This name underscores the truth that all authority and legacy ultimately come from God’s generous hand, encouraging trust in His sovereign provision and timing. It also points to the personal and relational nature of God’s giving, which is foundational for the Christian faith.
keyVerseReflection: 2 Kings 23:36 states, "Jehoiakim was twenty and five years old when he began to reign... And his mother's name was Zebudah, the daughter of Pedaiah of Rumah." The mention of Zebudah by name, emphasizing her identity as "given," highlights the providential role she played in the Davidic line. This detail enriches the verse by showing that Jehoiakim’s royal lineage is not only a matter of paternal descent but also connected to a mother whose name signifies a gift, reminding us that God’s sovereign gifts often come through ordinary human relationships.
